ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs, directors, managers, authorised representatives and corporate shareholders against the French Financial Sanctions lists issued by the Direction Générale du Trésor, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Sanctions List, and OFAC SDN List where a substantive US nexus is identified. PEP detection is required pursuant to Article L561-10 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, applying a three-step classification (family members, close associates, known public functions) combined with commercial databases (World-Check or Dow Jones) and TRACFIN guidance indicators. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all medium-risk and PEP-related profiles, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation. Negative news screening must be repeated independently before drafting and before registration, and recorded in a contemporaneous AML/CFT file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) accessible via INPI at data.inpi.fr; RCS database via Infogreffe; incorporation formalities filed through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use Latin script and may contain accented characters. Where the proposed name derives from a non-Latin alphabet or a foreign script, a validated transliteration into the Latin alphabet must be provided, accompanied by a certified French translation for formal filing. The name must be distinctive within the RCS, not deceptive or contrary to ordre public, and must not create a likelihood of confusion with existing registered marks or company names. For regulated activities, the name must not imply an authorisation that has not yet been obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS/INPI registrar refuses the proposed corporate name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the INPI within 30 days of notification, pursuant to Article R123-126 of the French Commercial Code. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may file a hierarchical appeal (recours hiérarchique) with the Direction des Services Judiciaires or bring an urgent jurisdictional application (référé) before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce / Tribunal judiciaire of the intended registered office. Where the rejection is based on a third-party trademark conflict, the applicant may contest through the INPI Opposition Division or seek a negotiated coexistence agreement with the trademark owner. The full appeal dossier must include the name clearance report, trademark search results, and proof of actual distinctive use or intended use plan.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-agent address is permissible only as a genuine commercial address physically located in France, providing registered-office services and mail receipt; it does not satisfy the French substance requirements for a venture capital general partner that falls within the scope of AMF authorisation as a société de gestion de portefeuille or AIFM under Articles L532-9 and L532-13 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. For such regulated entities, the AMF requires a real physical establishment, effective local management and sufficient compliance infrastructure; a virtual-only arrangement will automatically fail the regulatory fit-and-proper assessment. For a wholly unregulated holding GP entity, a registered office with commercial agent services may be accepted, but the ultimate beneficial owners must maintain material and effective management within France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For an AMF-regulated AIFM/VC GP manager, the likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by AMF, DGFIP or URSSAF is high (estimated 70% probability within the first two operating years). For a non-regulated venture capital holding GP entity, the inspection likelihood is moderate (estimated 30% probability), driven mainly by annual corporate tax audits, social contribution inspections and occasional judicial post-incorporation verification of registered-office commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution et statuts de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required for a SARL under French law; capital may be subscribed in cash or in kind and is freely determined by the shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of [Company Name] SARL, duly convened and holding a meeting on [Date] at [Address], unanimously adopts the following resolutions: 1. The initial share capital of EUR 1,000 is subscribed in full by the shareholder [Name] in cash. 2. The registered office is fixed at [Full Address in France]. 3. The following are appointed as officers: Gérant [Name], with full powers to represent the Company; Deputy Gérant [Name]. 4. The Board authorizes the opening of a corporate bank account at [Bank Name] and the execution of all incorporation documents. 5. The Gérant is empowered to file the Acte de Constitution with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and to publish the necessary announcements. This resolution is adopted in accordance with the draft Articles of Association and is effective immediately upon adoption.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — portal: impots.gouv.fr; entity formation filings through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL receives its statutory TIN automatically at incorporation: the Guichet Unique transmits the registration dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and to INSEE, which issues the 9-digit SIREN number and the SIRET establishment number. The DGFiP then assigns the intra-community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) for the SARL's main establishment. A foreign entity without a French establishment that needs a French VAT ID must file Form 15769 (or use the EU non-established VAT registration portal) with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), appointing a fiscal representative if required under Article 302 quater of the CGI. The SARL's tax ID is the SIREN/SIRET; the VAT ID is referenced on the French registration certificate (extrait Kbis) and in impots.gouv.fr login.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not use the US check-the-box system. A SARL defaults to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés or IS) on its French profit. It may irrevocably elect to be taxed as a partnership/pass-through (option pour l'impôt sur le revenu, Article 239 bis AA CGI) only if it meets the small-enterprise definition (fewer than 50 employees and annual turnover below €10 million for enterprises with commercial/industrial/artisanal activity, or €5 million for service activity); this IR option is limited to five years for existing SARLs. Alternatively, a family SARL (SARL de famille, Article 239 bis CGI) may opt for income tax with fiscal transparency among family members. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognised for French-tax-resident SARLs; anti-hybrid rules under ATAD/DAC6 disallow deduction/non-inclusion outcomes using hybrid instruments or entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SARL, VAT registration is mandatory when taxable turnover exceeds €85,000 for supplies of goods, €37,500 for supplies of services (including management fees from a venture capital fund), or €47,600 for certain legal and accounting services; a non-established foreign entity has no de minimis threshold and must register before the first taxable supply in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory e-invoicing (e-invoicing) and e-reporting under the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF). The rollout is staged: large taxpayers from 1 September 2026, mid-sized enterprises from 1 September 2027, and small entreprises from 1 September 2028. B2B transactions between French VAT-registered taxpayers must be transmitted via the PPF or an accredited PPF platform use-compatible API or Factur-X format. Customs export declarations, ESC (Déclaration d'Échange de Biens) filings, and VAT return reporting remain required; real-time fiscal clearance and digital stamping are not yet in force for standard goods exports, but the PPF platform demands machine-readable invoicing data for all domestic e-invoiced B2B transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union are eligible for 0% VAT (exonération à l'export) under Article 262-I of the French General Tax Code (CGI), provided the exporter is the established supplier, the goods physically leave the EU within the legally required delay (normally within 90 days from dispatch), and the exporter holds a valid customs export declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation or DEX) and transport documents. Services directly linked to exported goods (e.g., international carriage, loading, handling) and services supplied to non-EU recipients (delivered outside the EU) may also qualify for zero-rating or territorial exclusion under Articles 258-B and 259-A CGI. A venture capital GP's management fees for advising a non-EU fund are generally taxable in France unless the effective use and enjoyment is outside the EU and the service is not linked to French property; offshore services can be zero-rated only if all territoriality conditions in Article 259 CGI are strictly met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane DX/DEX or AAS status)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (transport document)
Inward Remittance Certificate (justifying receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or abusive zero-rating claims expose the SARL to retrospective VAT assessment with interest (intérêts de retard, Article 1727 CGI), a monetary penalty of 80% of the tax evaded for intentional concealment (Article 1729-a or 1729-b CGI), and criminal penalties for tax fraud (Article 1741 CGI) of up to €500,000 fine and up to five years' imprisonment in aggravated circumstances. The tax administration may also claw back refunded VAT credits and require a guarantee from the GP, and can apply a 100% penalty for trafficking in customs documents or fictitious invoices.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank, with foreign-exchange and capital-movement rules principally derived from European Union law, French monetary and financial law, the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, the Autorité des marchés financiers, and the French Treasury Directorate General.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general exchange controls on lawful current-account or capital-account transactions. The euro is freely convertible and cross-border dividend, interest, service-fee, loan, capital-contribution, and redemption payments are generally permitted through regulated payment institutions or banks. Remittances remain subject to corporate-law distributions, distributable-profit and statutory-reserve rules, transfer-pricing requirements, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner screening, sanctions controls, anti-money-laundering procedures, and documentary evidence of the underlying transaction. A SARL acting as a venture-capital general-partner or fund-management entity may require authorization or registration under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive framework, French Monetary and Financial Code rules, and AMF supervision, depending on whether it manages alternative investment funds, provides portfolio management, or performs regulated investment services. Foreign direct investment screening may apply to acquisitions or investments in sensitive French sectors; it is not a general restriction on ordinary capital funding of a French SARL. Payments involving sanctioned persons, high-risk jurisdictions, opaque ownership structures, or unexplained third-party funding may be delayed, rejected, or reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or prescribed deadline for converting export receipts into euros. Export receipts may remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the holder's discretion, subject to bank controls, accounting requirements, tax reporting, sanctions screening, and any contractual financing covenants. Goods and services exports must be supported by commercially credible invoices, contracts, customs records where applicable, and evidence of performance. Cross-border cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more into or out of the European Union require customs declaration by the person carrying the cash or equivalent instruments. Banks may request transaction-purpose information and may apply enhanced monitoring to fund-management fees, capital calls, distributions, and payments involving non-EU counterparties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank, together with the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
BPCE group bank, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne regional entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary treasury and payment operations; Low as the sole relationship bank for a regulated or potentially regulated venture-capital GP. An electronic-money institution or payment institution authorized in France or another European Economic Area state may provide euro payment accounts, safeguarding, SEPA transfers, and selected foreign-currency services under passporting or local authorization. It may not provide ordinary bank deposits, insured deposit-taking, unrestricted credit, or all correspondent-banking services. Offshore digital EMIs outside the European Economic Area generally cannot provide regulated payment services to French customers without an applicable French or EEA authorization, passport, or local agent arrangement. A fintech may reject investment-fund activity, pooled client money, capital-call proceeds, third-party collections, or payments involving high-risk jurisdictions. The company should maintain a regulated French or EEA bank as primary account provider and use an EMI only after confirming safeguarding, segregation, settlement, chargeback, sanctions, account-closure, and access-to-funds terms.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that directors physically attend a branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available using qualified or equivalent electronic identification, video verification, electronic signatures, and registry-source checks. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, notarized or apostilled documents, certified translations, live video interviews, or an enhanced compliance review. The legal representative, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and controlling persons should be prepared to participate. Capital-deposit accounts for incorporation may be opened subject to bank-specific procedures and issuance of a certificate of deposit; the account is normally converted into an operational account after registration and delivery of the definitive corporate extracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SARL is described as a venture-capital general partner or fund-management entity but its regulated-status analysis is unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a legal-regulatory memorandum identifying whether the company is an AIFM, portfolio management company, investment adviser, fund general partner, holding company, or administrative service provider; include AMF authorization or registration evidence where applicable, the relevant AIFM delegation arrangements, compliance officer details, organizational chart, and written confirmation of activities that are outside the regulated perimeter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee shareholders, layered holding companies, or an inability to identify ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the current Kbis extract, articles of association, shareholder register, ownership chart through every entity to natural persons, UBO declaration, passports and residential-address evidence for UBOs and directors, corporate authorization documents, and explanations for any trust, foundation, nominee, or intermediary structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funding originates from an offshore investor, investment fund, family office, or third party that is not the registered shareholder or contractual counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed subscription or capital-contribution documents, board and shareholder approvals, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, audited financial statements or investor capital-call notices, bank statements, beneficial-owner information for the funding vehicle, and a written explanation of the payment chain and economic purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity consists of large capital calls, fund distributions, investor subscriptions, or rapid pass-through payments inconsistent with ordinary SARL operating expenses.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the fund constitutional documents, limited-partner agreements, management agreements, capital-call notices, distribution waterfall, projected transaction volumes, counterparties by jurisdiction, payment-flow diagram, treasury policy, segregation-of-funds controls, reconciliation procedures, and evidence that client or investor money is not improperly commingled with corporate funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involve sanctioned, high-risk, secrecy, or heavily cash-based jurisdictions, or counterparties with adverse media.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide sanctions-screening results, country-risk assessment, counterparty KYC files, beneficial-owner verification, transaction contracts, invoices, investment committee approvals, enhanced due-diligence reports, source-of-funds evidence, and documented escalation and rejection procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The business plan, tax residence, registered office, management location, and expected payment geography are inconsistent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the registered-office lease or domiciliation agreement, management-services agreement, employee and director information, tax-registration evidence, operational budget, business plan, expected countries of activity, office and staffing evidence, and an explanation of any non-French management or investment entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank cannot verify the commercial rationale for management fees, carried interest, advisory fees, intercompany loans, or related-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide intercompany and management agreements, transfer-pricing policy, pricing support, invoices, board approvals, timesheets or service evidence, tax analysis, beneficial-owner checks, and accounting records demonstrating the actual services and arm's-length basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity has no completed annual accounts, newly incorporated status, or limited operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed twelve-to-thirty-six-month budget, funding commitments, incorporation documents, proof of initial capital, investor pipeline, signed mandates, management biographies, regulated-status evidence, expected monthly cash-flow schedule, and a designated compliance and accounting framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, virtual-asset platforms, unregulated brokers, or cash to fund corporate activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a transaction-history explanation, source-of-funds evidence, wallet or broker ownership verification where relevant, conversion records, tax treatment, board approval, and a remediation plan prohibiting personal-account and unapproved virtual-asset flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder capital, shareholder loans, and fund-related corporate funding through an account held in the SARL's legal name at a regulated French or EEA credit institution or payment institution. Use the legal entity's exact registered name, IBAN, BIC, registered address, and a consistent payment reference such as 'share capital contribution', 'shareholder loan under agreement dated [date]', or 'management-fee funding'. France does not operate a universal statutory purpose-code system equivalent to certain exchange-control jurisdictions; the bank may nevertheless require a payment purpose, underlying agreement, source-of-funds evidence, UBO information, and regulatory-status documentation. Capital contributions should be supported by the subscription decision, articles or amendment, deposit certificate requirements, and accounting entries. Shareholder loans should be documented with principal, maturity, interest, repayment terms, transfer-pricing support, and any French related-party or thin-capitalization analysis. Do not route investor money through the GP's unrestricted operating account where segregation, fund documentation, regulatory rules, or contractual obligations require a dedicated fund or client-money account. Reconcile all inbound wires to the general ledger and retain SWIFT messages, bank advices, agreements, and compliance evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border transfers, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 payment record, for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. Use a commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, open-account payment with trade-credit controls, or bank guarantee where the transaction involves goods, technology, customs exposure, or material counterparty risk. For investment-management operations, use contractual management-fee, administration, legal, accounting, software, and professional-service payments supported by invoices and executed agreements rather than trade documentation. Each payment file should contain the beneficiary's legal name, address, bank details, invoice or contract, sanctions-screening result, tax treatment, and approval record. Banks may request customs declarations, bills of lading, certificates of origin, proof of delivery, service evidence, or fund documents. Avoid unexplained third-party payments, split payments designed to evade controls, cash settlement, and payments to personal accounts. French and EU payment, AML, sanctions, VAT, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, and accounting rules apply independently of the selected clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards entered into with an authorized bank or investment firm for documented currency exposure, subject to suitability, appropriateness, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation, and EMIR obligations where applicable.

Non-deliverable forwards for non-convertible or restricted currencies, where offered by an authorized counterparty and used for a genuine underlying exposure; settlement, reporting, sanctions, market-abuse, and counterparty-risk controls are required.

Foreign-exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps for documented funding or liquidity exposures, subject to counterparty authorization, master documentation, collateral and margin terms, valuation controls, and applicable EMIR reporting or clearing requirements.

Currency options, collars, and participating forwards for hedging documented investor commitments, management-fee receipts, portfolio-company funding, or other forecast cash flows, subject to board-approved risk limits and product-governance controls.
Euro foreign-currency accounts and natural hedging through matching receipts and payments, subject to bank account terms, accounting treatment, and treasury segregation.

The SARL should not conduct proprietary speculative FX dealing, market the instruments to third parties, or provide investment services without the authorization required under French and EU financial-services law. Hedge accounting, valuation, derivatives disclosures, counterparty limits, and documentation should be established before execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' decision approving the SARL annual financial statements and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Partners of the SARL (internal corporate decision; not filed with a regulator)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of each fiscal year-end; calendar-year entity by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The manager of the SARL may be exposed to civil liability; unresolved failure to approve accounts may support a court order or judicial dissolution claim.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual statutory accounts with the commercial registry (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval and no later than seven months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year entity by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar's formal notice, court-ordered monetary penalty (astreinte), criminal fine for the manager, and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS for persistent failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation or update of the beneficial-owner declaration tied to the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual accounts filing; no later than seven months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year entity by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete corporate formalities may be rejected; inaccurate or omitted UBO declaration may result in fines, criminal liability, and commercial registry strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and financial statement annex (liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entity: second business day following 1 May; off-calendar fiscal year: within three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% plus late interest; intentional non-filing may be penalised at 40% and may trigger enforced tax recovery.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual regulatory report for the licensed venture-capital general partner (rapport annuel to the AMF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the deadline stipulated in the AMF authorisation, generally within four months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year entity typically by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AMF disciplinary proceedings, administrative fines, compliance restrictions, or suspension/withdrawal of the management-company licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint an independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if it exceeds at least two of three thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet EUR 4.0 million, annual net turnover EUR 8.0 million, and 50 average employees. An AMF-licensed venture-capital general partner is also required to appoint auditors for regulatory capital and annual financial reporting regardless of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (ANC/PCG) governs individual statutory accounts; consolidated financial statements, if prepared, may use IFRS as adopted by the EU. The licensed GP remains subject to AMF regulatory capital and accounting return rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a stand-alone annual UBO return for an existing SARL. The UBO declaration must be filed on incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership. At each annual accounts filing, the company must confirm through the Guichet Unique that the UBO declaration on file remains accurate, making the confirmation an annual event tied to the accounts-filing deadline. Any transfer of SARL parts must be recorded in the transfer register and, if the beneficial-owner data changes, the UBO declaration must be updated accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Officers
Register of Transfers of Parts Sociales

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard rate; reduced 15% on first €38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; effective rate rises to 25.825% for groups with annual turnover above €7,630,000 (3.3% social contribution).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Available preferential mechanisms: 15% reduced SME CIT on taxable profits up to €38,120; patent box taxation at 10% on net qualifying IP income; R&D tax credit (CIR) at 30% up to €100m and 5% above; innovation tax credit (CIP) at 20% for SME innovation expenses; carried interest may benefit from Art. 150-0 B ter within carried-interest regimes; tax losses, while available for indefinite carryforward, are capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income above that cap for any given fiscal year (the model input here uses the stated 5-year convention).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n° 2065 (Declaration de résultats des personnes morales) and supporting liasse fiscale (Form 2050 to 2059-SD), filed electronically on impots.gouv.fr via the TéléIS / EDI-TDFC portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; four quarterly prepayments (acomptes IS) due in principle on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December for calendar-year entities, with the balance paid with the return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: file by the second business day after 1 May. Any other fiscal year-end: generally file by the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal status (SARL), SIREN/SIRET, APE/NAF code (6499Z), registered office, tax representative identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the French permanent establishment address and the non-resident parent's tax identification; appoint a fiscal representative (where required) before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify main activity: venture capital General Partner management entity; enter gross revenue from management fees, carried interest allocations, and other operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State whether a 6.4X tax régime or carried-interest passthrough is claimed; do not include profits attributable to a foreign headquarters absent a French PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable profit before loss carryforward; reconcile accounting profit (Résultat comptable) with fiscal profit (Résultat fiscal).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File only the French-source share allocable to the French business; restrict the result to management fees billed in/by the French GP and to capital-gain allocations taxed in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter prior-year losses carried forward, deducting no more than the statutory cap (€1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim losses of French PEs under the same cap; cross-border losses of the foreign head office are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For a VC GP, detail carried interest profits, dividend participation income, and any subsidy/performance-linked income; permanent establishment attribution records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If applying for DTA credit, attach the foreign residence certificate and the French-source income calculation for each item.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report cross-border payments for services, royalties, interest and dividends subject to French withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify beneficial ownership and treaty/directive relief on the relevant schedule; the payor must retain the residence certificate for 6 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% of unpaid tax if less than 30 days late; 40% after 30 days; 80% for occult activity or abusive tax conduct; plus 0.20% per month late-payment interest on the aggregate tax due. Failure to file despite a formal notice also triggers a fixed fine of €150 to €1,500 depending on the form; no separate daily surcharge exists.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends distributed to non-residents under Article 119 bis CGI; 75% where the recipient's State is listed as non-cooperative (ETNC); treaty rates generally 0-15% (e.g. 15% under US-France for portfolio; 5% for qualified participations; 0% for certain EU parent-subsidiary situations).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taxpayer must be beneficial owner and hold the relevant residence certificate; the French paying entity files the reduced-rate application on the official token/fiscal representative procedure with the local tax centre, attaching the foreign residence certificate, shareholding and holding-period documentation, financial statements and a certificate of fiscal domicile (Cerfa No. 5000 is commonly used in reciprocal claims); if the full mitigation is not applied ex ante, refund is claimed by appeal to the Direction générale des Finances publiques before 31 December of the second calendar year following the withholding. In EU parent-subsidiary situations, withholding is exempt once the 5% participation threshold and 2-year holding period are met, subject to anti-abuse and substance review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% under Article 182 B CGI for industrial/commercial IP paid to non-French residents; DTA rates commonly 0%, 5% or 10% depending on treaty and IP type. Interest: domestic law generally imposes no withholding on ordinary bank/commercial interest to non-resident lenders; however, interest paid to non-cooperative state payees carries a 75% withholding; interest on profit-sharing or equity-convertible loans may be recharacterized and attracts the dividend or 33.33% regime.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 of French or consolidated group turnover triggers the formal Local File / Master File documentation obligation under Article L.13 AA LPF; CbC Report threshold EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue. A venture-capital GP below these thresholds must nevertheless be able to evidence benchmarking of management fees, carried interest and shareholder loans on request, and must include arm's-length pricing analysis in internal accounting records.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No separate ESR code exists in France; anti-abuse law and ATAD principles apply. For a VC GP, substance is evidenced by French registered office, a French-resident gérant, discretionary independence of the management committee, French payroll and bank accounts, minutes of meetings and traceable decision-making files. Artificial, nominal or mailbox-company arrangements will be challenged as abuse of rights (abus de droit) and may lose treaty/Directive benefits for lack of beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of carried interest, fictitious advisory fees, shell investors behind capital calls, or false accounting to avoid corporate income tax and social contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Increase of tax to 80% plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; criminal fine up to €75,000 for an individual and up to €375,000 for a legal entity acting through the manager, with imprisonment of up to 5 years; publication of the conviction and temporary suspension from public contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the corporate veil is allowed under Article L.267 LPF: a gérant who has committed serious, repeated misconduct or organized insolvency may be made personally liable for all unpaid corporate taxes and penalties, and may face travel bans, bans on managing any company (interdiction de gérer) and civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / False Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the Form 2065 liasse fiscale or the accompanying balance sheet within the applicable deadline, or filing a return with knowingly incomplete cross-border transaction schedules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of 10% if the delay is under 30 days; 40% if in excess of 30 days; 80% for hidden activity; automatic fixed fine of €150-€1,500; monthly interest at 0.20% on the underpaid tax and additional assessment penalties up to 80% for bad faith.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may order the manager to pay the company's tax debts where recovery through the company proves impossible; for false auditing of the GP, the gérant may also be criminally prosecuted for fiscal fraud and for presentation of inaccurate accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length management fees paid to a related foreign GP or holding, artificial reallocation of carried interest to a low-tax partner, or interest rates on shareholder loans materially different from market rates, unaccompanied by required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of cross-border income under Article 57 CGI; adjustment plus 40% penalty for deliberate failure to disclose, or 80% for abuse of law; in cases of incomplete deductible documentation, the administration may deny deduction for the unsubstantiated amount and the same penalties apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign non-arm's-length invoices or false registrations expose themselves to separate criminal sanctions, personal civil liability for resulting tax shortfall, and observation of the company's assets to attach management-company receivables.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law (ATAD and Beneficial Ownership)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: French SARL-GP used as a mailbox: no actual staff, no French decision-making, no French bank account, contracts signed from a tax-haven parent, and artificial circular financing via Swift capital-call wires to avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The administration will apply the abuse of rights procedure (Art. L.64 LPF), disregard the French entity, reallocate all income to the true beneficiary, impose the 80% penalty and deny treaty relief for lack of beneficial ownership; the entity may also be compulsorily dissolved as a fictitious company under commercial law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Accomplice directors are exposed to personal liability for the company's taxes and to criminal penalties for fictitious incorporation; individual response includes asset seizure, travel bans, and a prohibition from holding a management office for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of investor capital calls or carried-interest distributions to launder proceeds, process payments to shell investment vehicles, or conceal beneficial owners in the transfer chain via Swift transfers without proper KYC and TRACFIN declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French Monetary and Financial Code imposes criminal penalties of up to 5 years' imprisonment and €375,000 fine for laundering of capital derived from tax evasion, aggravated money laundering increases to 10 years and €750,000; in addition, corporate penalties and confiscation of the funds and profit-generating assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is subject to personal criminal proceedings, extended seizure of assets, travel bans, and professional disqualification; the supervisory authority may revoke any statutory AIFM license of the GP and the manager's own 'agrément' or declaration.
